title: Freddie Keppard at the Dreamland
summary: Keppard played with Palmer's band at Dreamland; his style, sweating, compared with Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Can you tell me about Freddie Keppard?
Did you play with him? He played with him. He played, he come with us at Deluxe. At not Deluxe, at Dream. And he played with us a while at Dream. That was a Dream one at 35th Street and State.

One out of West Harlem. Yeah, I sure was. And he played with us at Dream over here, see. And he was a good trumpet player. Nice trumpet player. He had one style of playing, though. He had jazz style, too, pretty good. But he didn't have it like so much of it as the other fellas, you know. He was very good, and he knew his instrument nice. And he put good tones in it. And that guy would get to playing sometimes and play in the melody and get to sweating. He was so fat, you know. Sweating? Yeah, he was so fat. By the time he started playing, he began to get sweating, you know. And Louis Armstrong does that, too, now, see. About six or eight handkerchiefs. He got to carry about eight handkerchiefs with him, see. I don't know. I don't know whether it's that beer or what it is, but whatever it is, they got it down, see. They used it with handkerchiefs, and mostly for sweating and getting my heart's in.
